question_stem:
A Hall probe is placed near to one end of a current-carrying solenoid, as shown in Fig. 9.1.

{{figure:9702_s17_42_q09_figure_9_1}}

Fig. 9.1

The probe is rotated about the axis $XY$ and is then held in a position so that the Hall voltage is maximum.

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.text: a Hall probe is made from a thin slice of material,

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text: in order for consistent measurements of magnetic flux density to be made, the current in the probe must be constant.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
The probe is now rotated through an angle of $360^{\circ}$ about the axis $XY$. At angle $\theta = 0$, the Hall voltage $V_{H}$ has maximum value $V_{MAX}$.

On Fig. 9.2, sketch the variation with angle $\theta$ of the Hall voltage $V_{H}$ for one complete revolution of the probe about axis $XY$.

{{figure:9702_s17_42_q09_figure_9_2}}

Fig. 9.2
